introduction: The `afspec` Go library provides an idiomatic Go implementation of the Python `afspec` library, enabling Go programs to load, validate, mutate, save, and render agent-fox specification packages with byte-for-byte round-trip fidelity. Note: requirements referencing `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` and `github.com/goccy/go-yaml` APIs are based on the PRD's verified external API surface and should be cross-checked against installed library versions before implementation.

glossary.BootstrapError: An error type returned when BootstrapSpec.Finalize fails due to missing artifacts or validation errors
glossary.BootstrapSpec: A struct that supports incremental population of spec artifacts with deferred cross-file validation before assembling a final Spec
glossary.BuildDependencyGraph: A standalone function that builds the inter-spec dependency graph from tasks.json declarations
glossary.CompleteSubtaskStates: A method on Tasks that marks all subtasks in specified groups as done, bypassing the state machine
glossary.ComputeCoverage: A method on TestSpec that computes test coverage by scanning test entries against requirements, properties, and paths
glossary.ComputeIntentHash: A standalone function that computes the SHA-256 hash of the normalized ## Intent section from a PRD body
glossary.CreateSpec: A standalone function that creates a new Spec with initialized sub-artifacts in draft state
glossary.DependencyEdge: A struct representing a directed dependency edge between two specs, carrying FromSpec, ToSpec, FromGroup, ToGroup, and Relationship fields
glossary.DependencyGraph: A struct representing the inter-spec dependency graph built from tasks.json declarations
glossary.DiscoverSpecs: A standalone function that scans a directory for spec directories and returns lightweight SpecMeta entries
glossary.EARS: Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax — a structured natural-language pattern for writing acceptance criteria
glossary.Finalize: The method on BootstrapSpec that assembles a Spec from all set artifacts and runs full validation without saving to disk
glossary.IntentError: An error type returned when ComputeIntentHash cannot find the ## Intent section in a PRD body
glossary.IntentHash: A SHA-256 hash computed over the normalized ## Intent section of a PRD body
glossary.IsSpecDirName: A standalone function that validates whether a directory name matches the NN_snake_case pattern
glossary.Kahn's algorithm: A topological sort algorithm that detects cycles by iteratively removing nodes with no incoming edges
glossary.LifecycleError: An error type returned when an invalid spec or subtask state transition is attempted
glossary.LoadError: An error type returned when a spec directory cannot be loaded due to missing required files or malformed content
glossary.LoadSpecLandscape: A standalone function that collects metadata for all specs for landscape views
glossary.MarshalJSON: A standalone function that produces deterministic JSON serialization matching Python's output byte-for-byte
glossary.MoveToArchive: A standalone function that transitions a spec to archived state and moves its directory to the archive subdirectory
glossary.ParseSpecDirName: A standalone function that parses a directory name matching the NN_snake_case pattern into its components
glossary.RenderCombined: A method on Spec that renders all artifacts as a single Markdown document
glossary.RenderEARSSentence: A method on Criterion that renders a single EARS criterion as a natural-language sentence
glossary.RenderIndividual: A method on Spec that renders each artifact separately as a map of filename to Markdown string
glossary.RenderIndividualScoped: A method on Spec that renders each artifact filtered to the refs of a target task group
glossary.ResetSubtaskStates: A method on Tasks that resets all subtasks in specified groups to pending
glossary.SaveError: An error type returned when a spec cannot be written to disk
glossary.Schemas: A standalone function that returns the bundled JSON Schema files as a map[string][]byte
glossary.SchemeURLLoader: A jsonschema interface implementation that loads schema documents from embedded bytes rather than the network
glossary.SpecError: The base error type for the afspec library; all specific error types wrap it
glossary.SpecMeta: A lightweight struct containing metadata parsed from a spec's PRD frontmatter, used for discovery
glossary.Supersede: A method on Spec that marks a sealed spec as superseded and prepends a deprecation banner to the PRD body
glossary.TopologicalSort: A method on DependencyGraph that returns spec IDs in dependency order using Kahn's algorithm
glossary.Transition: A method on Spec that transitions the spec's lifecycle state and persists the change to disk
glossary.TransitionSubtask: A method on Tasks that transitions a single subtask's state via the state machine
glossary.ValidTransition: A standalone pure function that checks whether a lifecycle state transition is allowed without side effects
glossary.ValidateCrossFile: A method on Spec that checks cross-file consistency including dangling references, coverage gaps, and ID format validation
glossary.ValidateCrossSpec: A standalone function that checks cross-spec interface consistency across multiple specs
glossary.ValidateSchema: A method on Spec that checks each artifact against bundled JSON Schema files and EARS/task-group structural rules
glossary.ValidateStructured: A method on Spec that returns validation results as a categorized map[string]any for CLI consumption
glossary.ValidationResult: A struct containing errors and warnings from spec validation, with a Valid boolean that is true when Errors is empty
glossary.active: A lifecycle state indicating a spec is in active use
glossary.afspec: The Go library (and its Python counterpart) for working with agent-fox specification packages
glossary.architecture.md: An optional Markdown artifact within a spec directory describing the spec's architecture
glossary.archived: A terminal lifecycle state indicating a spec has been moved to the archive directory
glossary.done: A terminal subtask state indicating the subtask has been completed
glossary.draft: The initial lifecycle state of a newly created spec
glossary.dropped: A terminal subtask state indicating the subtask will not be completed
glossary.frontmatter: YAML metadata block delimited by --- at the top of a prd.md file
glossary.go-cmp: The github.com/google/go-cmp package used for structured diffs in test failures
glossary.go-yaml: The github.com/goccy/go-yaml package used for parsing YAML frontmatter in prd.md
glossary.in_progress: A subtask state indicating the subtask is currently being worked on
glossary.jsonschema: The github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 package used for JSON Schema validation
glossary.pending: The initial subtask state indicating the subtask has not yet been started
glossary.pending_reevaluation: A subtask state indicating the subtask needs to be re-examined before proceeding
glossary.prd.md: The Product Requirements Document file within a spec directory, containing YAML frontmatter and a Markdown body
glossary.queued: A subtask state indicating the subtask is ready to be worked on
glossary.requirement_refs: A list of requirement IDs referenced by a subtask, used for scoped rendering
glossary.requirements.json: The JSON artifact within a spec directory containing structured requirements
glossary.round-trip fidelity: The property that a spec loaded and saved by the Go library produces byte-for-byte identical output to the Python library
glossary.sealed: A lifecycle state in which a spec cannot be mutated or saved
glossary.spec directory: A filesystem directory matching the NN_name pattern that contains a spec's artifacts
glossary.subtask: An individual unit of work within a task group, tracked with a state machine
glossary.superseded: A terminal lifecycle state indicating a spec has been replaced by another
glossary.tasks.json: The JSON artifact within a spec directory containing task groups and subtasks
glossary.test_spec.json: The JSON artifact within a spec directory containing test specifications
glossary.test_spec_refs: A list of test spec entry IDs referenced by a subtask, used for scoped rendering
glossary.testdata: The directory in the Go repository containing static spec fixture directories extracted from the Python test suite

requirements.title: LoadSpec — load spec artifacts from a directory

user_story.goal: call LoadSpec(dir) to load all spec artifacts from a directory into a Spec struct
user_story.benefit: so that I can work with spec data natively in Go without shelling out to Python

acceptance_criteria.action: reads prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, tasks.json, and optionally architecture.md, parses each artifact into the corresponding Go struct, and returns a populated Spec struct
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpec with a valid spec directory path

acceptance_criteria.action: parses the YAML frontmatter using yaml.Unmarshal and extracts the Markdown body separately, populating all frontmatter fields on the Spec struct
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) with frontmatter fields populated
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpec and prd.md contains YAML frontmatter delimited by ---

acceptance_criteria.action: loads all other required artifacts successfully and leaves the architecture field empty
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) with architecture field as empty string
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpec and architecture.md is absent from the directory

edge_cases.action: returns a LoadError identifying the missing file
edge_cases.error_condition: a required artifact (prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, or tasks.json) is missing from the directory

edge_cases.action: returns a LoadError wrapping the parse error
edge_cases.error_condition: a JSON artifact (requirements.json, test_spec.json, or tasks.json) contains malformed JSON

edge_cases.action: returns a LoadError wrapping the yaml.Unmarshal error with line/column info
edge_cases.error_condition: prd.md contains malformed YAML frontmatter (syntax error or type mismatch)

edge_cases.action: handles the missing delimiter in a manner that matches the Python implementation's behavior exactly
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, LoadError) or (*Spec, nil) matching Python behavior
edge_cases.error_condition: prd.md frontmatter is missing the closing --- delimiter

edge_cases.action: detects missing required fields post-parse and returns a LoadError
edge_cases.error_condition: prd.md frontmatter is present but required fields are missing after parsing

edge_cases.action: returns a LoadError wrapping the filesystem error
edge_cases.error_condition: the directory path does not exist or is not readable

requirements.title: Spec.Save — atomically write spec artifacts to disk

user_story.goal: call spec.Save(dir) to persist all spec artifacts atomically
user_story.benefit: so that partial writes never leave the spec directory in a corrupt state

acceptance_criteria.action: writes each artifact to a temporary file in the same directory, then renames each temp file to its final name atomically, producing output byte-for-byte identical to the Python library's output
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Save with a valid directory path on a non-sealed Spec

acceptance_criteria.action: refuses to write any files and returns a LifecycleError
acceptance_criteria.state: the Spec is in the sealed lifecycle state

edge_cases.action: cleans up any partially written temp files and returns a SaveError
edge_cases.error_condition: the target directory is not writable or the filesystem returns an error during temp file creation

edge_cases.action: removes the orphaned temp file and returns a SaveError
edge_cases.error_condition: the rename operation fails after the temp file is written (e.g., cross-device rename)

edge_cases.action: returns a SaveError without creating any files
edge_cases.error_condition: the directory path does not exist at save time

requirements.title: MarshalJSON — deterministic JSON serialization

user_story.goal: call MarshalJSON(v) to serialize a spec artifact to JSON
user_story.benefit: so that the output is byte-for-byte identical to the Python library's JSON output

acceptance_criteria.action: serializes struct fields in declaration order (matching JSON Schema property order) and sorts all map[string]T keys alphabetically using reflection-based custom marshaling
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns ([]byte, nil) with deterministic JSON output
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes MarshalJSON with a spec artifact struct

acceptance_criteria.action: produces output byte-for-byte identical to the Python library for every spec artifact type, including nested structs and map fields

edge_cases.action: returns an error from the marshaling step
edge_cases.error_condition: the input value contains a type that cannot be marshaled to JSON (e.g., a channel or function)

edge_cases.action: serializes the field as an empty JSON object {}
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ([]byte, nil) with {} for the empty map field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes MarshalJSON with a struct containing an empty map[string]T field

edge_cases.action: serializes the nil pointer as JSON null, matching Python's behavior
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ([]byte, nil) with null for the nil pointer field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes MarshalJSON with a struct containing a nil pointer field

requirements.title: Spec.Validate — full spec validation

user_story.goal: call spec.Validate() to check a loaded spec for errors and warnings
user_story.benefit: so that I can surface actionable feedback before using or publishing the spec

acceptance_criteria.action: runs schema validation, EARS constraint checks, task group structure rules, and cross-file consistency checks, then returns a ValidationResult with Valid set to true and empty Errors
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Validate on a fully valid spec

acceptance_criteria.action: collects all errors and warnings from schema and cross-file checks and returns a ValidationResult with Valid set to false
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Validate on a spec with one or more errors

edge_cases.action: returns a ValidationResult with Valid set to true and a non-empty Warnings slice
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Validate on a spec with warnings but no errors

edge_cases.action: validates without panicking and returns a ValidationResult
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Validate on a minimally populated spec (only required fields set)

requirements.title: Spec.ValidateSchema — JSON Schema and structural validation

user_story.goal: call spec.ValidateSchema() to check each artifact against bundled JSON Schema files
user_story.benefit: so that I can detect structural violations before cross-file checks

acceptance_criteria.action: compiles each bundled schema using jsonschema compiler with a SchemeURLLoader backed by embedded bytes, validates each artifact's JSON representation against its schema, and returns a ValidationResult with no errors
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateSchema on a structurally valid spec

acceptance_criteria.action: maps each *jsonschema.ValidationError to a ValidationResult error entry carrying InstanceLocation as path, KeywordLocation as keyword, and Message as the human-readable description
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateSchema and an artifact fails schema validation

edge_cases.action: returns a LoadError at startup when schemas are compiled, preventing the library from being used with corrupt schemas
edge_cases.return_contract: returns LoadError wrapping SpecError at initialization
edge_cases.error_condition: a bundled schema file is structurally invalid or contains a bad $ref (detected at compile time)

edge_cases.action: collects errors from all artifacts and returns them together rather than stopping at the first failure
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateSchema and multiple artifacts have schema errors

requirements.title: Spec.ValidateCrossFile — cross-file consistency checks

user_story.goal: call spec.ValidateCrossFile() to detect dangling references and coverage gaps across artifacts
user_story.benefit: so that I can ensure all cross-artifact references are consistent before publishing

acceptance_criteria.action: checks dangling references, coverage gaps, glossary completeness, and ID format validity across all artifacts and returns a ValidationResult with no errors
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateCrossFile on a spec with consistent cross-file references

acceptance_criteria.action: records a dangling reference error identifying the test entry ID and the missing requirement ID
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [{category: integrity, check: dangling_reference, ...}]}
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateCrossFile and a test spec entry references a requirement ID that does not exist in requirements.json

edge_cases.action: reports coverage gaps for all requirements that have no corresponding test entries
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ValidationResult with coverage gap warnings or errors for each uncovered requirement
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateCrossFile on a spec with no test entries

edge_cases.action: records an ID format validation error identifying the artifact and the malformed ID
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [{category: integrity, check: id_format, ...}]}
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateCrossFile and an ID in any artifact does not match the expected format

requirements.title: ValidateCrossSpec — cross-spec interface consistency

user_story.goal: call ValidateCrossSpec(specs, graph) to check interface consistency across multiple specs
user_story.benefit: so that I can detect API symbol mismatches and glossary conflicts before integration

acceptance_criteria.action: checks API symbol consistency, glossary conflicts, and contract mismatches across all provided specs using the dependency graph to determine which specs interact, and returns a ValidationResult
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns ValidationResult with Valid true if no cross-spec errors are found
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes ValidateCrossSpec with a slice of Spec values and a DependencyGraph

edge_cases.action: returns a ValidationResult with no errors since there are no cross-spec relationships to check
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes ValidateCrossSpec with a single spec (no dependencies)

edge_cases.action: records a glossary conflict error identifying both specs and the conflicting term
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [{category: integrity, check: glossary_conflict, ...}]}
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes ValidateCrossSpec and two specs define the same glossary term with different meanings

requirements.title: Spec.ValidateStructured — categorized validation output for CLI consumption

user_story.goal: call spec.ValidateStructured() to get validation results as a structured map
user_story.benefit: so that I can format and display validation output without parsing ValidationResult internals

acceptance_criteria.action: runs full validation and returns a map[string]any with a 'valid' key set to true, an 'errors' key set to an empty slice, and no 'warnings' key
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateStructured on a valid spec

acceptance_criteria.action: returns a map with 'valid' false and 'errors' containing entries with 'category' set to 'schema', 'message', 'artifact', and optionally 'path' and 'value' fields
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with schema errors

acceptance_criteria.action: returns a map with 'valid' false and 'errors' containing entries with 'category' set to 'integrity', 'message', 'check', and optionally 'requirement_id' fields
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with integrity errors

acceptance_criteria.action: includes a 'warnings' key in the returned map containing entries with 'category' set to 'warning', 'message', and 'entity_id' fields
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with warnings

edge_cases.action: omits the 'warnings' key from the returned map entirely
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with no warnings

requirements.title: Spec.Transition — lifecycle state transitions

user_story.goal: call spec.Transition(target, dir) to advance a spec's lifecycle state
user_story.benefit: so that I can manage spec lifecycle programmatically with persistence

acceptance_criteria.action: updates the spec's status field to the target state, persists the updated spec to disk, and returns the updated Spec
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) with status set to target state
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Transition with a valid target state and directory

acceptance_criteria.action: checks the transition table (draft→active, active→sealed, active→superseded, sealed→superseded, any→archived) and returns true if the transition is allowed, false otherwise, with no side effects
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes ValidTransition with a current and target state

edge_cases.action: returns a LifecycleError without modifying the spec or writing to disk
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes spec.Transition with a target state that is not a valid transition from the current state

edge_cases.action: returns a SaveError; the in-memory Spec copy reflects the new state but the on-disk state is unchanged due to atomic write semantics
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes spec.Transition and the disk write fails after the state is updated in memory

requirements.title: Spec.Supersede — mark a spec as superseded with deprecation banner

user_story.goal: call spec.Supersede(supersedingSpecID, dir) to mark a sealed spec as superseded
user_story.benefit: so that readers of the PRD are immediately informed of the replacement spec

acceptance_criteria.action: transitions the spec to the superseded state, prepends a deprecation banner referencing the superseding spec ID to the PRD body, and persists the updated spec to disk
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) with status superseded and deprecation banner in PRD body
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.Supersede with a superseding spec ID and directory on a sealed Spec

edge_cases.action: returns a LifecycleError without modifying the spec or writing to disk
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes spec.Supersede on a spec that is not in the sealed state

requirements.title: MoveToArchive — move a spec directory to the archive

user_story.goal: call MoveToArchive(specDir, root) to archive a spec
user_story.benefit: so that inactive specs are organized out of the active workspace

acceptance_criteria.action: transitions the spec to the archived state if not already archived, then moves the spec directory to {root}/archive/ using an atomic rename or copy-then-delete
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes MoveToArchive with a spec directory and root path

edge_cases.action: creates the archive directory before moving the spec, or returns a SaveError if creation fails
edge_cases.return_contract: returns nil on success or SaveError on failure
edge_cases.error_condition: the {root}/archive/ directory does not exist

edge_cases.action: returns a SaveError identifying the conflict without overwriting the existing archive entry
edge_cases.error_condition: a spec directory with the same name already exists in {root}/archive/

requirements.title: DiscoverSpecs — scan a root directory for spec directories

user_story.goal: call DiscoverSpecs(root) to enumerate all spec directories under a root path
user_story.benefit: so that I can build landscape views and dependency graphs without knowing spec locations in advance

acceptance_criteria.action: scans the root directory for subdirectories matching the NN_snake_case pattern, parses the PRD frontmatter of each, and returns a slice of SpecMeta entries with SpecID, SpecName, Status, and Dir fields populated
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes DiscoverSpecs with a root directory path

edge_cases.action: skips the malformed entry and continues scanning, collecting errors to return alongside the valid SpecMeta entries
edge_cases.return_contract: returns ([]SpecMeta, []error) where errors list the skipped directories
edge_cases.error_condition: a subdirectory matches the NN_snake_case pattern but its prd.md is missing or malformed

edge_cases.action: returns an empty slice and a LoadError
edge_cases.error_condition: the root directory does not exist or is not readable

edge_cases.action: returns an empty slice with no error
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes DiscoverSpecs on a root directory with no matching subdirectories

requirements.title: BuildDependencyGraph — build inter-spec dependency graph

user_story.goal: call BuildDependencyGraph(metas, root) to construct the dependency graph from tasks.json declarations
user_story.benefit: so that I can determine build order and detect circular dependencies across specs

acceptance_criteria.action: reads tasks.json for each spec, extracts cross-spec dependency declarations, and returns a DependencyGraph with Edges, Dependencies, Dependents, and TopologicalSort methods
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BuildDependencyGraph with a slice of SpecMeta and a root path

acceptance_criteria.action: returns spec IDs in topological order using Kahn's algorithm such that every spec appears before its dependents
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort on an acyclic graph

acceptance_criteria.action: detects the cycle using Kahn's algorithm and returns an error identifying the cycle
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort on a graph with a cycle

edge_cases.action: returns a DependencyGraph with no edges
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (*DependencyGraph, nil) with empty Edges slice
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes BuildDependencyGraph with a single SpecMeta (no dependencies)

edge_cases.action: records the dangling reference as an error and returns it alongside the partial graph
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (*DependencyGraph, error) with the partial graph and a descriptive error
edge_cases.error_condition: a tasks.json references a spec ID that is not present in the provided SpecMeta slice

requirements.title: IsSpecDirName and ParseSpecDirName — directory name validation and parsing

user_story.goal: call IsSpecDirName(name) and ParseSpecDirName(name) to validate and parse spec directory names
user_story.benefit: so that I can reliably identify spec directories without duplicating the matching logic

acceptance_criteria.action: returns true
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes IsSpecDirName with a string matching the NN_snake_case pattern

acceptance_criteria.action: returns false
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes IsSpecDirName with a string that does not match the NN_snake_case pattern

acceptance_criteria.action: returns the numeric prefix and the snake_case name portion as separate values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (string, string, nil) — numeric prefix, name, nil error
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes ParseSpecDirName with a valid NN_snake_case directory name

edge_cases.action: returns an error indicating the name is not a valid spec directory name
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes ParseSpecDirName with a string that does not match the NN_snake_case pattern

edge_cases.action: returns false
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes IsSpecDirName with an empty string

requirements.title: LoadSpecLandscape — collect metadata for all specs

user_story.goal: call LoadSpecLandscape(root, includeArchive, currentSpecID) to get a landscape view of all specs
user_story.benefit: so that I can display cross-spec context without loading full spec artifacts

acceptance_criteria.action: scans all spec directories including the archive subdirectory, parses PRD frontmatter for each, and returns a slice of SpecMeta entries excluding the currentSpecID entry
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpecLandscape with a root path, includeArchive true, and a currentSpecID

acceptance_criteria.action: scans only non-archived spec directories and returns SpecMeta entries for active and draft specs
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpecLandscape with includeArchive false

edge_cases.action: returns an empty slice with no error
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes LoadSpecLandscape and the root directory contains no spec directories

requirements.title: Tasks.TransitionSubtask — subtask state machine transitions

user_story.goal: call tasks.TransitionSubtask(subtaskID, target) to advance a subtask's state
user_story.benefit: so that I can track work progress through a well-defined state machine

acceptance_criteria.action: looks up the subtask by ID, verifies the transition is in the allowed table (pending→queued, pending→dropped, queued→in_progress, queued→pending, queued→dropped, in_progress→done, in_progress→pending_reevaluation, done→pending_reevaluation, pending_reevaluation→pending, pending_reevaluation→dropped), updates the subtask state, and returns the updated Tasks
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes tasks.TransitionSubtask with a subtask ID and a valid target state

edge_cases.action: returns a LifecycleError without modifying any subtask state
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes tasks.TransitionSubtask with a target state not in the allowed transition table for the subtask's current state

edge_cases.action: returns a LifecycleError identifying the missing subtask ID
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes tasks.TransitionSubtask with a subtask ID that does not exist in the Tasks struct

requirements.title: Tasks.CompleteSubtaskStates and Tasks.ResetSubtaskStates — bulk subtask state mutation

user_story.goal: call tasks.CompleteSubtaskStates(groupIDs) or tasks.ResetSubtaskStates(groupIDs) to bulk-update subtask states
user_story.benefit: so that I can mark entire task groups as done or reset them without iterating subtasks individually

acceptance_criteria.action: sets every subtask in each specified group to the done state, bypassing the state machine transition rules, and returns the updated Tasks
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes tasks.CompleteSubtaskStates with a slice of group IDs

acceptance_criteria.action: sets every subtask in each specified group to the pending state, bypassing the state machine transition rules, and returns the updated Tasks
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes tasks.ResetSubtaskStates with a slice of group IDs

edge_cases.action: skips the missing group ID and processes all valid group IDs, returning the updated Tasks without error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (*Tasks, nil) with valid groups updated
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes tasks.CompleteSubtaskStates or tasks.ResetSubtaskStates with a group ID that does not exist

edge_cases.action: returns the Tasks unchanged without error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (*Tasks, nil) with no state changes
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes tasks.CompleteSubtaskStates or tasks.ResetSubtaskStates with an empty groupIDs slice

requirements.title: Spec.RenderCombined and Spec.RenderIndividual — Markdown rendering

user_story.goal: call spec.RenderCombined() or spec.RenderIndividual() to render spec artifacts as Markdown
user_story.benefit: so that I can produce human-readable documentation from spec data

acceptance_criteria.action: renders all artifacts (PRD body, requirements, test spec, tasks, architecture if present) as a single concatenated Markdown document
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns string containing the full Markdown document
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderCombined

acceptance_criteria.action: renders each artifact separately and returns a map keyed by artifact name (e.g., 'prd', 'requirements', 'test_spec', 'tasks', 'architecture') to its Markdown string
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns map[string]string with one entry per artifact
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividual

edge_cases.action: omits the 'architecture' key from the returned map
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividual on a spec with no architecture.md

edge_cases.action: renders the requirements section as an empty or placeholder section without panicking
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderCombined on a spec with empty requirements

requirements.title: Spec.RenderIndividualScoped — task-group-scoped rendering

user_story.goal: call spec.RenderIndividualScoped(targetGroup) to render artifacts filtered to a task group's references
user_story.benefit: so that I can provide focused context to an AI agent working on a specific task group

acceptance_criteria.action: collects all requirement_refs and test_spec_refs from every subtask in targetGroup, renders only the referenced requirements (including acceptance criteria and edge cases whose IDs appear in requirement_refs), renders only the referenced test entries, renders the target group with full subtask detail and all other groups as one-line completion summaries, and includes PRD body and architecture unfiltered
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns map[string]string with scoped content per artifact
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividualScoped with a targetGroup that has requirement_refs and test_spec_refs

acceptance_criteria.action: falls back to full unscoped rendering equivalent to spec.RenderIndividual
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns map[string]string with full unscoped content
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividualScoped with a targetGroup that has no requirement_refs or test_spec_refs

acceptance_criteria.action: includes a Spec Overview listing all requirement IDs and titles for context, even for requirements not in the scoped set
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns map[string]string where the requirements entry includes a Spec Overview section
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividualScoped and the requirements section is scoped

edge_cases.action: falls back to full unscoped rendering and returns the result without error
edge_cases.return_contract: returns map[string]string with full unscoped content
edge_cases.error_condition: a caller invokes spec.RenderIndividualScoped with a targetGroup ID that does not exist in the Tasks struct

requirements.title: EARS Criterion Builders — convenience constructors for EARS criteria

user_story.goal: call UbiquitousCriterion, EventDrivenCriterion, ComplexEventCriterion, StateDrivenCriterion, UnwantedCriterion, or OptionalCriterion to construct EARS criterion structs
user_story.benefit: so that I can build requirements programmatically without manually setting pattern-specific fields

acceptance_criteria.action: returns a Criterion struct with the ears_pattern field set to the corresponding pattern and all provided arguments mapped to the correct struct fields
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns Criterion with ears_pattern and all relevant fields populated
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes any EARS criterion builder with valid arguments

acceptance_criteria.action: set only the fields relevant to each pattern (e.g., UnwantedCriterion sets error_condition but not trigger, state, or feature; OptionalCriterion sets feature but not trigger, state, or error_condition)

edge_cases.action: returns a Criterion with an empty ID field; validation of the ID is deferred to spec.Validate
edge_cases.return_contract: returns Criterion with empty ID field
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes any EARS criterion builder with an empty id string

requirements.title: BootstrapSpec — incremental spec population with deferred validation

user_story.goal: use NewBootstrapSpec(specID, specName) and BootstrapSpec.Finalize() to build a spec incrementally
user_story.benefit: so that I can populate artifacts one at a time and validate the complete spec only when ready

acceptance_criteria.action: returns a BootstrapSpec with the specID and specName set and all artifact fields empty
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes NewBootstrapSpec with a specID and specName

acceptance_criteria.action: assembles a Spec from all set artifacts, runs full schema and cross-file validation, and returns the assembled Spec with no validation errors
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) — nil slice indicates no errors
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BootstrapSpec.Finalize after setting all required artifacts

acceptance_criteria.action: returns nil for the Spec and a slice of ValidationError entries each with rule set to 'bootstrap' and message set to 'Missing artifact: {name}' for each missing artifact
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BootstrapSpec.Finalize with one or more required artifacts missing

acceptance_criteria.action: returns nil for the Spec and a slice of ValidationError entries describing the validation failures
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes BootstrapSpec.Finalize and all required artifacts are present but validation fails

edge_cases.action: each call assembles and validates independently; the BootstrapSpec is not mutated by Finalize
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (*Spec, nil) or (nil, []ValidationError) on each call independently
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes BootstrapSpec.Finalize multiple times on the same BootstrapSpec

edge_cases.action: returns all missing artifact errors and all validation errors together in the returned slice
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes BootstrapSpec.Finalize and both missing artifacts and validation errors are present

requirements.title: Schemas — return bundled JSON Schema files

user_story.goal: call Schemas() to access the embedded JSON Schema files
user_story.benefit: so that I can inspect or use the schemas without reading from the filesystem

acceptance_criteria.action: returns the map of schema file names to their raw bytes as embedded via //go:embed from the schemas/ directory
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns map[string][]byte with one entry per schema file
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes Schemas

edge_cases.action: always returns a non-nil map; the map is never empty because schema files are embedded at compile time and their absence would be a build error

requirements.title: ComputeIntentHash — SHA-256 hash of the PRD Intent section

user_story.goal: call ComputeIntentHash(body) to compute a stable hash of the PRD's Intent section
user_story.benefit: so that I can detect when the intent of a spec has changed

acceptance_criteria.action: extracts and normalizes the ## Intent section text, computes its SHA-256 hash, and returns the hex-encoded hash string
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes ComputeIntentHash with a PRD body string containing a ## Intent section

edge_cases.action: returns an IntentError indicating the section is missing
edge_cases.error_condition: the PRD body does not contain a ## Intent section

edge_cases.action: returns an IntentError since no ## Intent section can be found in an empty body
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes ComputeIntentHash with an empty string

requirements.title: TestSpec.ComputeCoverage — compute test coverage against requirements

user_story.goal: call ts.ComputeCoverage(req) to determine which requirements are covered by test entries
user_story.benefit: so that I can identify gaps in test coverage before publishing a spec

acceptance_criteria.action: scans all test entries against requirement IDs, correctness property IDs, and execution path IDs in the Requirements struct and returns a coverage report indicating which entities are covered and which are not
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a coverage report struct or map with covered and uncovered entity IDs
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes ts.ComputeCoverage with a Requirements struct

edge_cases.action: returns a coverage report indicating 100% coverage (no requirements to cover)
edge_cases.return_contract: returns coverage report with empty uncovered list
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes ts.ComputeCoverage with an empty Requirements struct

edge_cases.action: returns a coverage report indicating 0% coverage with all requirement IDs in the uncovered list
edge_cases.return_contract: returns coverage report with all requirement IDs in uncovered list
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes ts.ComputeCoverage with a TestSpec that has no test entries

requirements.title: CreateSpec — create a new spec with initialized artifacts

user_story.goal: call CreateSpec(specID, specName) to create a new Spec in draft state
user_story.benefit: so that I can start a new spec without manually initializing each artifact

acceptance_criteria.action: returns a Spec with status set to draft, all sub-artifacts initialized to their zero/empty values, and specID and specName set from the arguments
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns *Spec with status draft and all artifacts initialized
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller invokes CreateSpec with a specID and specName

edge_cases.action: returns a Spec with the empty values set; validation of the ID and name is deferred to spec.Validate
edge_cases.return_contract: returns *Spec with empty specID or specName fields
edge_cases.trigger: a caller invokes CreateSpec with an empty specID or specName

requirements.title: Error type hierarchy — SpecError wrapping and errors.As traversal

user_story.goal: use errors.As and errors.Is to inspect errors returned by the afspec library
user_story.benefit: so that I can handle specific error types while also catching all afspec errors with a single base type check

acceptance_criteria.action: implement the error interface and wrap SpecError such that errors.As(err, &SpecError{}) returns true for any LoadError, SaveError, LifecycleError, IntentError, or BootstrapError value
implement errors.As traversal from specific to base type: errors.As(loadErr, &LoadError{}) returns true, and errors.As(loadErr, &SpecError{}) also returns true for the same error value

edge_cases.action: never calls os.Exit or panics in response to invalid input; all error conditions are signaled via return values following Go's (result, error) convention, since the library is consumed by CLI and server programs that must handle errors gracefully

requirements.title: Round-trip fidelity — byte-for-byte output matching Python library

user_story.goal: load a spec with LoadSpec and save it with spec.Save and get byte-for-byte identical output to the Python library
user_story.benefit: so that Go and Python tools can interoperate on the same spec directories without corruption

acceptance_criteria.action: produces byte-for-byte identical JSON output to the Python library for all artifact types, verified by golden-file tests in testdata/ that load each fixture via LoadSpec, save to a temp directory, and compare output byte-for-byte using go-cmp
produces byte-for-byte identical PRD frontmatter output to the Python library using the hand-written renderer with fixed field order and explicit value formatting, not yaml.Marshal

edge_cases.action: outputs the full go-cmp diff (expected vs. actual) to the test log and fails the test, identifying the exact field or formatting rule that diverges
edge_cases.return_contract: test fails with human-readable diff in test log
edge_cases.trigger: a golden-file test detects a byte-level difference between Go output and the Python fixture

requirements.title: Concurrency model — no goroutine-safety guarantees

user_story.goal: understand the concurrency contract of the afspec library
user_story.benefit: so that I can synchronize access to Spec instances correctly in concurrent programs

acceptance_criteria.action: treats Spec structs as value types — mutation methods return new Spec copies rather than modifying the receiver in place, matching the Python immutable Pydantic model pattern
provides no goroutine-safety guarantees; callers are responsible for synchronizing concurrent access to Spec instances externally

edge_cases.action: documents the lack of goroutine-safety in package-level godoc so that callers are not surprised by data races under concurrent use

correctness_properties.title: LoadSpec and Save are inverse operations
correctness_properties.invariant: LoadSpec(dir) followed by spec.Save(tmpDir) produces byte-for-byte identical files to the originals in dir for all artifacts

correctness_properties.title: MarshalJSON is deterministic
correctness_properties.invariant: MarshalJSON(v) called twice on the same value returns identical byte slices

correctness_properties.title: ValidTransition is consistent with Transition
correctness_properties.for_any: current state and target state pair
correctness_properties.invariant: if ValidTransition(current, target) returns false then spec.Transition(target, dir) returns a LifecycleError; if ValidTransition returns true then spec.Transition succeeds (assuming no I/O errors)

correctness_properties.title: Validate Valid field is consistent with Errors
correctness_properties.invariant: ValidationResult.Valid is true if and only if ValidationResult.Errors is empty

correctness_properties.title: TransitionSubtask only allows defined transitions
correctness_properties.for_any: subtask in any state and any target state not in the allowed transition table
correctness_properties.invariant: tasks.TransitionSubtask returns a LifecycleError and leaves the subtask state unchanged

correctness_properties.title: BootstrapSpec.Finalize returns nil Spec on any error
correctness_properties.for_any: BootstrapSpec with any combination of set and missing artifacts
correctness_properties.invariant: if BootstrapSpec.Finalize returns a non-empty error slice then the returned Spec pointer is nil; if the error slice is nil then the Spec pointer is non-nil

correctness_properties.title: errors.As traverses from specific to base error type
correctness_properties.for_any: any error returned by the afspec library
correctness_properties.invariant: errors.As(err, &SpecError{}) returns true for every non-nil error returned by any afspec function or method

correctness_properties.title: TopologicalSort order is consistent with dependency edges
correctness_properties.invariant: for every DependencyEdge (FromSpec, ToSpec) in the graph, ToSpec appears before FromSpec in the slice returned by TopologicalSort

correctness_properties.title: Sealed specs cannot be saved
correctness_properties.for_any: Spec in the sealed lifecycle state
correctness_properties.invariant: spec.Save returns a LifecycleError and no files are written to disk

correctness_properties.title: map keys are always sorted in MarshalJSON output
correctness_properties.for_any: spec artifact struct containing one or more map[string]T fields
correctness_properties.invariant: the JSON output of MarshalJSON has all map keys in alphabetical order regardless of insertion order

execution_paths.title: Load, validate, and save a spec round-trip

steps.action: calls LoadSpec(dir) with a valid spec directory path
reads prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, tasks.json, and optionally architecture.md from the directory
parses YAML frontmatter from prd.md using yaml.Unmarshal and extracts the Markdown body
unmarshals each JSON artifact into the corresponding Go struct
returns a populated *Spec to the caller
calls spec.Validate() to check the loaded spec
runs ValidateSchema and ValidateCrossFile and returns a ValidationResult
calls spec.Save(tmpDir) to persist the spec
serializes each artifact using MarshalJSON and the hand-written PRD renderer
writes each artifact to a temp file then renames atomically to the final path
observes byte-for-byte identical output files in tmpDir compared to the original dir

execution_paths.title: Discover specs and build dependency graph

steps.action: calls DiscoverSpecs(root) with a workspace root path
scans root for subdirectories matching the NN_snake_case pattern
parses PRD frontmatter from each matching directory and returns a []SpecMeta
calls BuildDependencyGraph(metas, root) with the returned SpecMeta slice
reads tasks.json for each spec and extracts cross-spec dependency declarations
constructs a DependencyGraph with all edges and returns it
calls DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort() to determine build order
runs Kahn's algorithm and returns spec IDs in dependency order or an error if a cycle is detected
observes the ordered spec ID slice for use in sequential processing

execution_paths.title: Bootstrap a new spec incrementally and finalize

steps.action: calls NewBootstrapSpec(specID, specName) to create a BootstrapSpec
returns a *BootstrapSpec with specID and specName set and all artifact fields empty
sets requirements, test spec, tasks, and PRD artifacts on the BootstrapSpec
calls BootstrapSpec.Finalize()
checks that all required artifacts are set; returns (nil, []ValidationError) if any are missing
assembles a Spec from all set artifacts
runs full schema and cross-file validation on the assembled Spec
returns (*Spec, nil) on success or (nil, []ValidationError) on failure
observes the assembled and validated *Spec or the list of validation errors

execution_paths.title: Transition a spec through its lifecycle and archive it

steps.action: calls CreateSpec(specID, specName) to create a new draft Spec
returns a *Spec with status draft and initialized artifacts
calls spec.Transition('active', dir) to advance to active state
calls ValidTransition('draft', 'active') to verify the transition is allowed
updates the status field and persists the spec to disk atomically
returns the updated *Spec with status active
calls spec.Transition('sealed', dir) to advance to sealed state
updates status to sealed and persists atomically
calls MoveToArchive(specDir, root) to archive the spec
transitions the spec to archived state and moves the directory to {root}/archive/
observes the spec directory at {root}/archive/{specDir}

execution_paths.title: Transition subtask states through the state machine

steps.action: calls LoadSpec(dir) to load a spec with tasks
returns a *Spec with a populated Tasks struct containing subtasks in pending state
calls tasks.TransitionSubtask(subtaskID, 'queued')
verifies pending→queued is in the allowed transition table
returns updated *Tasks with the subtask in queued state
calls tasks.TransitionSubtask(subtaskID, 'in_progress')
verifies queued→in_progress is allowed and returns updated *Tasks
calls tasks.TransitionSubtask(subtaskID, 'done')
verifies in_progress→done is allowed and returns updated *Tasks
calls spec.Save(dir) to persist the updated task states to disk

execution_paths.title: Render a spec scoped to a target task group

steps.action: calls LoadSpec(dir) to load a spec
returns a *Spec with requirements, test spec, and tasks populated
calls spec.RenderIndividualScoped(targetGroup) with a task group ID
collects all requirement_refs and test_spec_refs from every subtask in targetGroup
renders only the referenced requirements with a Spec Overview listing all requirements
renders only the referenced test entries
renders targetGroup with full subtask detail and all other groups as one-line summaries
includes PRD body and architecture unfiltered
observes a map[string]string with scoped Markdown content per artifact

error_handling.condition: LoadSpec is called with a directory missing a required artifact
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LoadError) wrapping SpecError; the LoadError message identifies the missing file name

error_handling.condition: LoadSpec encounters malformed JSON in any artifact
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LoadError) wrapping the JSON parse error and SpecError

error_handling.condition: LoadSpec encounters malformed YAML frontmatter in prd.md
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LoadError) wrapping the yaml.Unmarshal error with line/column info and SpecError

error_handling.condition: Spec.Save is called on a sealed Spec
error_handling.behavior: returns LifecycleError wrapping SpecError without writing any files

error_handling.condition: Spec.Save encounters a filesystem error during temp file creation or rename
error_handling.behavior: cleans up any partially written temp files and returns SaveError wrapping SpecError

error_handling.condition: Spec.Transition is called with an invalid target state
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LifecycleError) wrapping SpecError without modifying the spec or writing to disk

error_handling.condition: Tasks.TransitionSubtask is called with a transition not in the allowed table
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LifecycleError) wrapping SpecError without modifying any subtask state

error_handling.condition: Tasks.TransitionSubtask is called with a subtask ID that does not exist
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LifecycleError) wrapping SpecError identifying the missing subtask ID

error_handling.condition: BootstrapSpec.Finalize is called with one or more required artifacts missing
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, []ValidationError) where each missing artifact produces a ValidationError with rule 'bootstrap' and message 'Missing artifact: {name}'

error_handling.condition: ComputeIntentHash is called with a PRD body that has no ## Intent section
A bundled JSON Schema file is structurally invalid or has a bad $ref at compile time
error_handling.behavior: returns LoadError wrapping SpecError at library initialization, preventing use of the library with corrupt schemas

error_handling.condition: Spec.Supersede is called on a spec that is not in the sealed state
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, LifecycleError) wrapping SpecError without modifying the spec or writing to disk

error_handling.condition: MoveToArchive encounters a naming conflict in the archive directory
error_handling.behavior: returns SaveError wrapping SpecError without overwriting the existing archive entry

error_handling.condition: DiscoverSpecs is called with a root directory that does not exist or is not readable
BuildDependencyGraph encounters a tasks.json that references an unknown spec ID
error_handling.behavior: returns (*DependencyGraph, error) with the partial graph and a descriptive error identifying the dangling reference

error_handling.condition: DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort detects a cycle in the dependency graph
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, error) describing the cycle; the error message identifies the specs involved

error_handling.condition: MarshalJSON is called with a value containing an unmarshalable type (channel, function)
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, error) from the marshaling step

symbols.name: UnmarshalJSON
symbols.notes: Loads a schema document from embedded bytes. Returns parsed schema value; returns error on malformed JSON.

symbols.name: Compiler.Compile
symbols.notes: Compiles a schema URL against the loader. Returns *jsonschema.Schema; returns error if $ref resolution fails or schema is structurally invalid.

symbols.name: Schema.Validate
symbols.notes: Validates a JSON value against the compiled schema. Returns nil on success; returns *jsonschema.ValidationError on failure — a tree of errors each carrying InstanceLocation, KeywordLocation, and Message.

symbols.name: Unmarshal
symbols.notes: Parses frontmatter bytes into a Go struct or map[string]interface{}. Returns error with line/column info on syntax errors or type mismatches. Used exclusively for parsing YAML frontmatter in prd.md; yaml.Marshal is NOT used for writing.

symbols.name: Diff
symbols.signature: func Diff(x, y interface{}, opts ...Option) string
symbols.notes: Used in golden-file tests to produce human-readable structured diffs between expected fixture content and actual Save output. An empty string return indicates no difference.
